html:
Pakistan's main stock exchange, founded in Karachi in September 1947, weeks after the country's independence. In 2016 it merged with the Lahore and Islamabad exchanges to form the Pakistan Stock Exchange.

At Partition, the subcontinent's big markets, such as the Bombay Stock Exchange, all fell in India. Karachi, then Pakistan's capital and only big port, became the centre of its banking and business, and the new country needed its own market. The exchange began with only a handful of listed companies.

It grew with Pakistan's economy, slowly and through many swings tied to politics, wars and military rule. Its KSE-100 index, launched in 1991, became the main gauge of the market. After the 2016 merger, a group of Chinese exchanges bought a large stake in the new Pakistan Stock Exchange, part of China's deepening economic ties with Pakistan under the Belt and Road Initiative.
sum: Pakistan's main stock exchange, founded in Karachi in September 1947, weeks after the country's independence. In 2016 it merged with the Lahore and Islamabad exchanges to form the Pakistan Stock Exchange.
